name: xAI Colossus Supercomputer
summary: One of the world's largest single-site AI training clusters, built inside a former Electrolux manufacturing plant in southwest Memphis with rapid expansion into neighboring Southaven, MS.

power.note: Scaled rapidly from ~150 MW initial phase toward 1.0–1.2+ GW across the Memphis/Southaven cluster, supplemented by on-site natural gas turbines while utility substations were built.

water.coolingType: Liquid / Evaporative (Greywater treatment plant under construction)
water.note: Exact annual consumption is undisclosed; local utility filings cite hundreds of thousands to over 1M gallons/day peak cooling demand from the Memphis Sand Aquifer, with xAI funding a greywater recycling plant to reduce aquifer draw.

land.note: Repurposed ~785,000 sq ft former industrial factory expanding to ~2.6M sq ft across adjacent industrial parcels.

gridContext: TVA (Tennessee Valley Authority) + MLGW, plus temporary behind-the-meter methane gas turbines.
localBenefits: Revitalized a long-vacant industrial factory site in southwest Memphis.
Significant local property tax base expansion and high-profile AI investment in Shelby County.
Funded a dedicated greywater recycling facility intended to offset municipal potable aquifer usage.
localConcerns: Deployed dozens of unpermitted temporary natural gas turbines on-site, prompting Clean Air Act complaints from the NAACP and Southern Environmental Law Center over smog (NOx) and formaldehyde in an already burdened neighborhood (Boxtown).
Community and conservation groups (Protect Our Aquifer) raised alarm over pumping from the Memphis Sand Aquifer, the city's primary drinking water source.
Speed of rollout outpaced typical public environmental review and utility transparency.
